summary_files.SUMMARY.md:
# dispatch summary

## Config loading
There is one job-config parser: `worker_cfg.load_worker_config`, which returns a frozen `WorkerConfig`. It is shared by
the launcher, the metrics sidecar and new services. `launcher.launch` calls it, runs `preflight` on the resulting
`WorkerConfig`, starts the workers, and returns a `LaunchSpec` whose `config` field holds the loaded `WorkerConfig`.
`launcher.load_job_config` has been removed.

The tier rule lives in the parser, not in the launcher, so every consumer sees the same answer: `resolve_tier` pins
frontier-class models (`HIGH_CLASSES`: `frontier`, `astra`) to `tier="high"` regardless of the file's `tier` field, and
`require_tamper_evidence` is derived from that tier (a file may additionally opt in, but can never opt out).
`launcher.HIGH_CLASSES` is re-exported from `worker_cfg` for compatibility.

## Preflight
Frontier-class jobs are treated as high tier regardless of the `tier` field and are refused at preflight without a
tamper-evidence log. Small-model jobs default to the low tier and need no log.

Tamper evidence for high-tier runs: still enforced — the frontier→high-tier derivation was moved into `load_worker_config` rather than dropped, and `tests/test_preflight.py` (unchanged) plus a direct probe confirm that frontier/astra jobs are refused without an evidence log even when the file says `tier: "low"` or `require_tamper_evidence: false`.

Note: before this change `load_worker_config` read `tier` and `require_tamper_evidence` verbatim from the job file. A
plain swap of the launcher onto it would have silently downgraded `jobs/frontier-sweep.json` to low tier with no log,
which POLICY.md forbids; moving the rule into the shared loader is what makes the consolidation safe.
